[[File:Pete Muldoon.jpg|thumb|right|Pete Muldoon was the Blackhawks first head coach.]]
The [[Chicago Blackhawks]] are an American professional [[ice hockey]] team based in [[Chicago]], [[Illinois]]. They play in the [[Central Division (NHL)|Central Division]] of the [[Western Conference (NHL)|Western Conference]] in the [[National Hockey League]] (NHL).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nhl.com/ice/teams.htm|title=Teams|publisher=[[National Hockey League]]|access-date=2009-06-15|archive-date=2009-03-11|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090311030113/http://www.nhl.com/ice/teams.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref> The team was first named the "Chicago Black Hawks", until 1986, when spelling found in the original franchise documents spelled the franchise name as the "Chicago Blackhawks", making the team change its name in response.<ref>Diamond, Dan (1991). ''The Official National Hockey League 75th Anniversary Commemorative Book''. Toronto: McClelland & Stewart. p. 291. {{ISBN|0-7710-6727-5}}</ref> The team is also referred to as the "Hawks".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://blackhawks.nhl.com/team/app/?service=page&page=NewsPage&articleid=424652|title=This Month In Hawks History: June|publisher=National Hockey League|work=[[Chicago Blackhawks]]|access-date=2009-06-15|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090606184622/http://blackhawks.nhl.com/team/app/?service=page&page=NewsPage&articleid=424652|archive-date=2009-06-06}}</ref> The Blackhawks began their NHL play in the [[1926–27 NHL season|1926–27 season]] as an [[expansion team]] with the [[Detroit Red Wings|Detroit Cougars]] and the [[New York Rangers]], and is one of the [[Original Six]] teams.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nhl/columns/story?id=2773591|title=Do Original Six teams still matter in the NHL?|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=2007-02-23|access-date=2009-06-15|archive-date=2012-10-25|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121025115304/http://sports.espn.go.com/nhl/columns/story?id=2773591|url-status=live}}</ref> The franchise has 6 [[Stanley Cup]] [[List of Stanley Cup champions|championships]], most recently winning in the 2014–15 season. Having played in the [[Chicago Coliseum]] (1926–1929) and the [[Chicago Stadium]] (1929–1994), the Blackhawks have played their home games at the [[United Center]] since 1994. The Blackhawks are owned by the [[Wirtz Corporation]], chaired by [[Danny Wirtz]]; [[Kyle Davidson]] serves as the team's [[general manager]]. The Blackhawks named [[Nick Foligno]] as captain in the [[2024–25 NHL season|2024–25 season]], following the team's decision to not re-sign [[Jonathan Toews]] for the [[2023–24 NHL season|2023–24 season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://blackhawks.nhl.com/team/frontoffice.htm|title=Front Office|publisher=National Hockey League|work=Chicago Blackhawks|access-date=2009-06-15|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090806063156/http://blackhawks.nhl.com/team/frontoffice.htm|archive-date=2009-08-06}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://blackhawks.nhl.com/team/app?service=page&page=TeamPlayers&type=roster&location=/roster |title=Roster |publisher=National Hockey League |work=Chicago Blackhawks |access-date=2009-06-15 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090627024618/http://blackhawks.nhl.com/team/app?service=page&page=TeamPlayers&type=roster&location=%2Froster |archive-date=2009-06-27 }}</ref>

There have been 42 [[head coach]]es for the Blackhawks. The franchise's first head coach was [[Pete Muldoon]], who coached for 44 games in the [[1926–27 NHL season|1926–27 season]]. However, he is also well remembered for allegedly "[[Curse of Muldoon|putting a curse]]" on the Blackhawks, which stipulated that the team would never finish in first in the NHL.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://blackhawks.nhl.com/history/themclaughlinyears.htm |title=The McLaughlin Years |publisher=National Hockey League |work=Chicago Blackhawks |access-date=2009-06-16 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090106232331/http://blackhawks.nhl.com/history/themclaughlinyears.htm |archive-date=January 6, 2009 }}</ref> The Blackhawks never had a first-place finish until 40 years after that incident.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hockey-reference.com/teams/CHI/|title=Chicago Blackhawks|publisher=Sports Reference LLC|work=Hockey-Reference.com|access-date=2009-06-16|archive-date=2008-12-03|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081203222103/http://www.hockey-reference.com/teams/CHI/|url-status=live}}</ref> [[Hughie Lehman]], originally the team's goaltender, became the Blackhawks' third head coach after yelling at the first Blackhawks owner, [[Frederic McLaughlin]], that his proposed plays were "the craziest bunch of junk [he had] ever seen".<ref>{{cite book|title=Without Fear: Hockey's 50 Greatest Goaltenders|last=Allen|first=Kevin |author2=Duff, Bob |author3=Bower, Johnny |author3-link=Johnny Bower |year=2002|publisher=[[Random House|Triumph Books]]|location=[[Chicago]]|isbn=978-1-57243-484-4 |oclc=49936232|page=59}}</ref>

[[Orval Tessier]] became the only head coach to have been awarded the [[Jack Adams Award]] with the Blackhawks by winning it in the [[1982–83 NHL season|1982–83 season]].<ref name="adams">{{cite web|url=http://www.nhl.com/trophies/adams.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080706102444/http://www.nhl.com/trophies/adams.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=2008-07-06|title=Jack Adams Award|publisher=National Hockey League|access-date=2009-06-16}}</ref> [[Tommy Gorman]], [[Tommy Ivan]], and [[Rudy Pilous]] are the only Blackhawks head coaches to have been elected to the [[Hockey Hall of Fame]] as a [[List of members of the Hockey Hall of Fame#Builders|builder]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.legendsofhockey.net:8080/LegendsOfHockey/jsp/LegendsMembersByYear.jsp?type=Builder|title=Hockey Hall of Fame inductees&nbsp;— Builders by Induction Year|publisher=[[Hockey Hall of Fame]]|access-date=2009-06-16|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090528120538/http://www.legendsofhockey.net:8080/LegendsOfHockey/jsp/LegendsMembersByYear.jsp?type=Builder|archive-date=2009-05-28}}</ref>  Gorman, [[Bill Stewart (sports official)|Bill Stewart]], Pilous, and [[Joel Quenneville]] are the only coaches to have won a Stanley Cup championship as the head coach of the Hawks.<ref name="champs">{{cite web|url=http://www.nhl.com/cup/champs.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090629213230/http://www.nhl.com/cup/champs.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=2009-06-29 |title=Stanley Cup Champions and Finalists |publisher=National Hockey League |access-date=2009-06-15 }}</ref>

[[Billy Reay]], the Blackhawks' head coach for 14 seasons, is the franchise's all-time leader for the most regular-season and playoff games coached and wins, with 1012 regular-season games coached, 516 regular-season game wins, 117 playoff games coached, and 57 playoff game wins. Twenty-three head coaches spent their entire NHL head coaching careers with the Blackhawks. [[Darryl Sutter]] and [[Brian Sutter]] are the only pair of brothers<ref>{{cite news|url=https://calgaryherald.com/Sports/Brent+Sutter+cites+family+explaining+resignation+Devils+coach/1679048/story.html|title=Brent Sutter cites family in explaining resignation as Devils coach|work=[[Calgary Herald]]|date=2009-06-09|access-date=2009-06-16}} {{Dead link|date=October 2010|bot=H3llBot}}</ref> to have coached the Blackhawks; both coached the Hawks for three seasons each.

Joel Quenneville was the head coach of the Blackhawks from the [[2008–09 NHL season|2008–09 season]] to early in the [[2018–19 NHL season|2018–19 season]].<ref name="Quenneville fired">{{cite web |title=RELEASE: Blackhawks make coaching change |url=https://www.nhl.com/blackhawks/news/release-blackhawks-make-coaching-change-301652676 |website=NHL.com |access-date=November 6, 2018 |date=November 6, 2018 |archive-date=November 7, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181107010220/https://www.nhl.com/blackhawks/news/release-blackhawks-make-coaching-change/c-301652676 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nhl/news/story?id=3646685|title=Blackhawks fire Savard after 4 games, hire Quenneville|publisher=ESPN|date=2008-10-16|access-date=2009-06-16|archive-date=2008-11-04|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081104201951/http://sports.espn.go.com/nhl/news/story?id=3646685|url-status=live}}</ref> and guided the Blackhawks to three Stanley Cup titles in [[2010 Stanley Cup Finals|2010]], [[2013 Stanley Cup Finals|2013]] and [[2015 Stanley Cup Finals|2015]]. At the time of his firing, Quenneville was the second-winningest coach both in the Blackhawks and NHL history, and was also second in [[List of NHL statistical leaders#Regular season games coached|all-time games coached]].<ref name="Quenneville fired" />

The current coach of the Blackhawks is [[Jeff Blashill]], who was named head coach on May 22, 2025.<ref name="Blashill">{{cite web |title=RELEASE: Jeff Blashill Named 42nd Head Coach in Blackhawks History |url=https://www.nhl.com/blackhawks/news/release-jeff-blashill-named-42nd-head-coach-in-blackhawks-history |website=NHL.com |access-date=May 23, 2025 |date=May 22, 2025}}</ref>
